name: Scott Walker
label: 4AD
lede: Noel Scott Engel had a teen-idol fan club bigger than the Beatles' at 23, spent a decade singing other people's songs to get out of contracts, and finished on 4AD with a percussionist punching a side of pork.

eras.title: Noel Engel, child actor, session bassist
eras.text: Before he was a Walker he was a boy on Broadway and on Eddie Fisher's TV show, then a Los Angeles teenager who loved Stan Kenton, Bill Evans and Bergman films. He played bass for hire and found a partner who'd take him to London.

years.h: Eddie Fisher takes up a boy singer from Broadway
years.p: Born Noel Scott Engel in Hamilton, Ohio, in 1943, he's been in Pipe Dream and Plain and Fancy by the time his family settles in California. Fisher puts him on his TV show more than once.
years.xp: A single called 'Misery' tried to make him a teen idol. In Los Angeles he fell for cool jazz, Stan Kenton and Bill Evans, and for Bergman, Fellini and Bresson. He went to Hollywood Professional School, then art school, and worked as a session bassist while still a teenager.

years.src: Wikipedia: Scott Walker · Wikipedia: The Walker Brothers
years.h: Three unrelated men become the Walker Brothers
years.p: Engel met John Maus in 1961, after playing with the Routers; they backed Maus's sister and toured as a fake Surfaris. Drummer Gary Leeds joins in 1964, and his father pays for the trip to Britain.

eras.title: Bigger than the Beatles, for a minute
eras.text: In England, the baritone took over. Two No. 1s, a fan club that outgrew the Beatles' and a frontman who couldn't stand any of it.

years.cap: The Walker Brothers on Thank Your Lucky Stars, 1965
years.src: Wikipedia: The Walker Brothers · Wikipedia: Scott Walker
years.h: The Walker Brothers land in London
years.p: 'Pretty Girls Everywhere', with John singing, goes nowhere. 'Love Her', sung by Scott, makes the top 20, and he becomes the voice of the group.

years.cap: The Walker Brothers on Top of the Pops, 1965
years.h: 'Make It Easy on Yourself' goes to No. 1
years.p: A Bacharach and David ballad with a wall of strings. It tops the UK chart and reaches No. 16 in the US.
years.xp: The sound was Phil Spector's wall of sound with British orchestrations, often arranged by Ivor Raymonde. Johnny Franz was the named producer, but Wikipedia credits Scott as co-producer in practice.

years.cap: Scott, John and Gary Walker at the BBC's Lime Grove Studios, c. 1966
years.src: Wikipedia: Scott Walker · Wikipedia: The Walker Brothers
years.h: 'The Sun Ain't Gonna Shine Anymore' is No. 1
years.p: The second chart-topper. The fan club grows past the Beatles' own.

years.h: Walker is found unconscious in his London flat
years.p: Wikipedia reports a suicide attempt: the gas stove on and the windows shut. Walker rarely talked about his private life afterwards.

years.cap: Scott Walker with the German support band the Magics on the Walker Brothers' 1967 tour
years.src: Wikipedia: Scott Walker · Wikipedia: The Walker Brothers
years.h: The Walker Brothers split
years.p: John's influence had faded and the two fell out. Scott told a journalist he drank a bottle of wine and a bottle of Scotch a day to roughen a voice he thought too sweet.
years.xp: That April the group had topped a UK package tour with [[Jimi Hendrix|06fb1c8b-566e-4cb2-985b-b467c90781d4]], Cat Stevens and Engelbert Humperdinck on the bill.

years.cap: Scott Walker signing an autograph in London, 1967
years.h: Scott launches the solo career, Brel songs and all
years.p: An instant hit. Alongside his own songs are Jacques Brel's, in Mort Shuman's English translations.

eras.title: Brel, Bergman and a monastery
eras.text: At the height of his fame Walker went to study Gregorian chant with Benedictine monks and came back writing his own songs. By the fourth album the public had stopped following.

years.src: Wikipedia: Scott Walker · Wikipedia: The Walker Brothers
years.h: Scott 2 goes to No. 1 in Britain
years.p: The single 'Joanna' makes the top 20. The Walker Brothers briefly reunite for a tour of Japan.

years.cap: Scott Walker recording for Dutch TV's Fenklup, June 7, 1968
years.h: A pop star studies Gregorian chant at Quarr Abbey
years.p: Walker stays with the Benedictine monks at Quarr Abbey on the Isle of Wight, and digs into lieder and modern classical music.

years.cap: Scott Walker singing on television, c. 1969
years.h: The BBC gives Walker his own TV series, Scott
years.p: Ballads, big band standards, Brel and his own songs. Almost no footage survives; the audio came out in 2019 as Live on Air 1968–1969.
years.xp: A covers album of the TV songs followed, with no originals on it. Manager Maurice King, Wikipedia says, wanted the next Andy Williams or Frank Sinatra.

years.h: Scott 4, credited to Scott Engel, misses the chart
years.p: His first album of entirely his own songs, released under his birth name. It doesn't chart and is soon deleted.
years.xp:
Walker said the album tried to "link lyrics by Sartre, Camus and Yevtushenko to Bartok modal lines." Some have guessed the birth-name credit hurt sales; every reissue since has said Scott Walker.

Out of print for over twenty years, it came back on CD in 1992 and has been praised ever since, by [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] among others.

years.h: Side one his, side two covers
years.p: 'Til the Band Comes In splits the difference. His last new songs until Nite Flights in 1978.

eras.title: Lost years, then The Electrician
eras.text: Four albums of film tunes, standards and country, made to clear a contract. Then a Walker Brothers reunion, a hit, and a last record so dark it pointed at everything he did later.

q: I was acting in bad faith for many years.
years.src: Wikipedia: Scott Walker · Wikipedia: Scott Walker: 30
years.h: Four albums without a single Scott Walker song
years.p: The Moviegoer, Any Day Now, Stretch and We Had It All (1972–74) are film themes, easy listening and country. Walker later disowned them and kept them off CD.
years.xp: He called this stretch his "lost years," made "by rote, just to get out of contract," with drink for consolation. BGO put out Stretch and We Had It All on CD in the late 1990s without his permission.

years.cap: The reunited Walker Brothers in Denmark, 1975
years.h: The Walker Brothers reunite; 'No Regrets' reaches No. 7
years.p: The Tom Rush cover is a hit, but the No Regrets album stops at No. 49 and two singles from Lines miss the chart.

years.h: With the label going under, the Walker Brothers make Nite Flights
years.p: Each man writes his own songs. Scott's four open the record, among them 'The Electrician', about a CIA torturer at work.
years.xp: They were his first new songs since 1970. Critics liked the record; it sold as badly as Lines, the tour stuck to the old hits, and the group drifted apart. Walker wasn't seen in public for six years.

eras.title: Virgin, Julian Cope and Climate of Hunter
eras.text: Dire Straits' manager got him a deal, Julian Cope made him a cult hero, and the album that came out of it sounded like nothing he'd made before. It didn't sell, and the next one was abandoned.

years.h: Dire Straits' manager signs Walker to Virgin
years.p: Ed Bicknell takes him on. Five years pass before the next album.

years.h: Julian Cope compiles The Godlike Genius of Scott Walker
years.p: Fire Escape in the Sky, chosen by Julian Cope for Zoo Records, reaches No. 14 on the UK indie chart and gets critics listening again.

years.src: Wikipedia: Climate of Hunter · Wikipedia: Scott Walker
years.h: Mark Knopfler and Billy Ocean play on Climate of Hunter
years.p: Half the songs are numbers ('Track Three', 'Track Five'). It reaches No. 60, and the planned tour never happens.
years.xp:
Producer [[Peter Walsh|8821570c-fc1e-4dd6-81f5-130b9f161b6c]], fresh from [[Simple Minds|f41490ce-fe39-435d-86c0-ab5ce098b423]], says the musicians recorded their parts without hearing the melodies. Walker kept them "a closely guarded secret" so nobody would play to them.

Free-improv saxophonist Evan Parker is on it too. NME put it in its top five albums of 1984.

years.h: Sessions with Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois are scrapped
years.p: A second Virgin album, with [[Brian Eno|ff95eb47-41c4-4f7f-a104-cdc30f02e872]] and Daniel Lanois producing and Robert Fripp on guitar, is abandoned after early sessions. Virgin drops him.

eras.title: Tilt, and a modernist composer appears
eras.text: Reissues brought a new generation to the 1960s records just as Walker went somewhere much stranger. Tilt was the first part of what he called a trilogy.

years.h: A best-of reaches No. 4, and Scott 1 to 4 arrive on CD
years.p: No Regrets: The Best of Scott Walker and The Walker Brothers 1965–1976 goes top five, and the solo albums get their first CD releases.
years.xp: The next year [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]] covered the Walker Brothers' 'Nite Flights' on Black Tie White Noise.

years.h: Eleven years on, Tilt
years.p: Orchestra, industrial percussion, and songs about Pasolini's murder, cockfighting and the Gulf War. It reaches No. 27 in the UK on Fontana.
years.xp:
Most of it was written in 1991–92 and recorded at RAK and the Townhouse, co-produced with Peter Walsh. Drag City put it out in the US in 1997.

Pitchfork's Jazz Monroe, years later: "Scarily, maddeningly good."

years.h: A Bond song and a Léos Carax score
years.p: Walker sings David Arnold's 'Only Myself to Blame' for The World Is Not Enough and writes the soundtrack to Carax's Pola X.

years.h: Walker curates Meltdown and doesn't sing
years.p: He runs the South Bank Centre festival and writes music for a Richard Alston dance piece, Thimblerigging.

years.h: A standing ovation at the Q Awards
years.p: [[Jarvis Cocker|38550441-d437-4aff-867e-e79bf0c04142]], whose band [[Pulp|76b2e842-5e85-4c97-ab62-d5bc315595b5]] Walker had produced on 2001's We Love Life, presents the award. Only Phil Spector and Brian Eno had received it before.

eras.title: 4AD, and the pork
eras.text: An independent label signed a man in his sixties and got the most extreme records of his life: The Drift, Bish Bosch, and an album with a drone-metal band.

years.h: 4AD signs Scott Walker
years.p: The label that started with post-punk singles takes him on. He tells interviewers he wants to make records faster.

years.cap: Scott Walker in a press photo for The Drift, 2006
years.src: Wikipedia: The Drift · Wikipedia: Scott Walker
years.h: The Drift takes 17 months at Metropolis
years.p: Songs about torture, Srebrenica, Mussolini and Clara Petacci, and Elvis's stillborn twin. The orchestra gets one day at AIR.
years.xp: The sounds include a braying donkey and a demonic Donald Duck impression. Vaughan Oliver at v23 designed the sleeve. Metacritic averaged 85.

years.cap: Scott Walker in the studio during the Drift sessions
years.src: Wikipedia: Scott Walker: 30 · Wikipedia: Scott Walker
years.h: On film, a percussionist punches a joint of pork
years.p: Stephen Kijak's Scott Walker: 30 Century Man premieres at the London Film Festival, with [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]] as executive producer and footage of the Drift sessions.
years.xp: Bowie, [[Brian Eno|ff95eb47-41c4-4f7f-a104-cdc30f02e872]], [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]], [[Damon Albarn|7d7a5fdd-0d04-4c36-8bee-906feeae239c]], Marc Almond, Sting and Johnny Marr are among those interviewed. Grant Gee shot it. Adam Yauch's Oscilloscope released it in North America in 2009.

years.cap: Scott Walker in a 4AD press photo for Bish Bosch, 2012
years.h: Machetes and shofars on Bish Bosch
years.p: Seventy-three minutes, his longest record. The centrepiece runs 21:41 and follows Zerco, Attila's jester, until he becomes a brown dwarf.
years.xp:
The writing took just over a year, "lightning speed" for him, though he said he still "had to wait and wait" for the words. The title is British slang for job done, plus Hieronymus Bosch.

'The Day the "Conducator" Died' is a Christmas song about Ceaușescu's execution. Walker called Tilt, The Drift and Bish Bosch "kind of a trilogy."

years.h: Sunn O))) haul their amps to London for Soused
years.p: In 2009 Walker turned down [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]]'s invitation to sing on Monoliths & Dimensions. After Bish Bosch he called them.
years.xp:
He sent wordless synth demos showing exactly where the guitar drones should go. "I could get those gaps, you see, between phrases... but now I had the drones," Walker said.

He wanted to call it Ronronner, French for purr; Stephen O'Malley, who lives in France, thought it too cute. Metacritic averaged 83.

years.h: Walker scores Brady Corbet's The Childhood of a Leader
years.p: His first film score since Pola X. Corbet hires him again for Vox Lux in 2018.

years.h: Sundog collects his lyrics
years.p: Six sections, from the 1960s to new songs, with a foreword by novelist Eimear McBride.

eras.title: Titan, at 76
eras.text: Walker died in London in March 2019. The tributes came from the artists who'd grown up on him.

years.cap: Scott Walker in a late-career 4AD portrait
years.h: Scott Walker dies in London at 76
years.p: 4AD announces it three days later, giving cancer as the cause and calling him a "unique and challenging titan." [[Thom Yorke|8ed2e0b3-aa4c-4e13-bec3-dc7393ed4d6b]], Marc Almond and Neil Hannon pay tribute.

years.h: The Brutalist is dedicated to Walker
years.p: Brady Corbet, who gave Walker his last two film scores, dedicates his 2024 film to him.
